title: Equipment & Vehicle Loans Held by One Member
content:
**Standard.** A member may hold any number of Equipment & Vehicle Loans; each financed purchase is its own loan with its own schedule, rate and collateral, and units bought together from one seller on one bill of sale are financed on one loan. There is no cap on the number of loans held (no per-member maximum is set); how loans held together interact is set by the cross-collateral clause of the security agreement.

## The standard restated

| Question | Answer under the standard |
|---|---|
| How many equipment loans may one member hold? | Any number; no maximum per member. |
| Does each financed purchase get its own loan? | Yes — its own schedule, rate and collateral. |
| Units bought together from one seller on one bill of sale | Financed on one loan. |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A member who buys a combine and a grain head from one dealer on one bill of sale finances both units on one loan, with one schedule and one rate.
- The same member who later buys a semi tractor from a different seller finances it as a separate loan with its own schedule, rate and collateral; holding the first loan does not limit the second.
